source: Fuyuki Ebata. Causative and passive in Sakha: Focusing on double-accusative causative and impersonal passive. Томский журнал ЛИНГ и АНТР . Tomsk Journal LING & ANTHRO. 2013. 2 (2)
notes: Sakha passive suffix -IlIn can be attached to some intransitive stems. In this case also, the person/number marking in the predicate is always 3SG, and we cannot posit an overt subject. Namely, the resultant is also an impersonal passive. Unlike passives from transitives, Sakha impersonal passives from intransitives are used only for describing a state of affairs, as in (38) and (39).
en: One cannot easily go into such a place.
